national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today stated that India is taking every step needed to become a preferred destination for the semiconductor industry. Inaugurating SEMICON India 2026 at Yashobhoomi in New Delhi today, Mr Modi said the world is looking for new and trusted manufacturing destinations and India is steadily preparing itself to meet this need. Mr Modi highlighted that India’s semiconductor ecosystem is expanding rapidly and opening new opportunities for innovation, investment and growth.. He discussed how the explosive demand for Artificial Intelligence is shifting the focus from mere transistor size to holistic system integration, including memory placement and heat management. Mr Modi said that on one side India’s economy is growing and the other side, global trust in India is also growing. He said, despite the challenging global environment, India recorded a growth rate of 7.8 per cent. Prime Minister said, at the same time, Japan’s credit rating agency also upgraded India’s sovereign rating. Mr Modi said, every citizen of the country is working with a commitment to build a developed India. Prime Minister said, India’s semiconductor ecosystem is expanding rapidly and it is is opening new opportunities for innovation, investment and growth. Prime Minister Modi said, India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 expanded outlay to 13.5 billion US dollar from eight billion US dollar in the first phase. He highlighted that so far 12 chip making projects have been approved in the next phase it will further increase. In his address, the Prime Minister also mentioned about recently held BRICS Summit in New Delhi. He said, India successfully hosted the summit in which New Delhi Declaration was adopted with consensus of every member country. Mr Modi said, it is another major testament to the world’s trust in India. He said, young talents who are researching in India should come forward. Mr Modi said, the youth who are researching abroad should also join the development of advanced technologies in India. He urged industry leaders to spearhead Research and Development in the country. He added that this will be mutually beneficial, driving industry growth while empowering India’s youth. On the occasion, Union Minister of Electronics and IT Ashwini Vaishnaw said that India had wanted to establish a semiconductor industry for several decades, but it was possible only under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He said, the foundation has now been laid and the next step is to build the industry through Semicon 2.0, which focuses on six major pillars. This include semiconductor design, machines and materials, memory, silicon, compound and logic fabrication units and research and development. He said, the government has set a target to support at least 200 startups and companies to design chips in India across the spectrum of semiconductor requirements. Minister of State for Electronics and IT Jitin Prasada, Secretary S Krishnan, officials, delegations were present on the occasion. The SEMICON India 2026 event has brought together over 600 exhibitors, 300 international companies, and delegations from more than 50 countries. The exhibition features six country pavilions representing Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Netherlands, Singapore and Sweden, twelve State Government pavilions, and a dedicated Startup Pavilion.The conference and exhibition, being held from today is being organised on the theme Silicon to Systems: Building the Ecosystem. It has brought together global and Indian companies, policymakers, investors, researchers, start-ups, academic institutions and students from across the semiconductor and electronics value chain.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | National 19 SEMICON 2.0 expected to generate up to one lakh employment opportunities: Union Minister Ashwini ...
national_raw_news.content: Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology Ashwini Vaishnaw today said that SEMICON 2.0 is expected to generate around one lakh crore rupees investment into the semiconductor industry in the coming times. Addressing the media at SEMICON India 2026 in New Delhi, Mr Vaishnaw said that India’s design capability is known across the world. He said that the approach under SEMICON 2.0 will be to promote semiconductor design companies. He noted that the SEMICON 2.0 is also expected to generate up to one lakh employment opportunities. Highlighting the second pillar of SEMICON 2.0 – Machines and Materials, the Minister said that many machine makers and capital equipment makers are participating in the event and are looking to set up their bases in India. He said that those engaged in manufacturing will have the opportunity to connect with the precision manufacturing ecosystem developing in the country. Mr Vaishnaw also informed that under SEMICON 1.0, around four hundred universities and institutes are already teaching chip design to their students. He said the government is now looking forward to upgrading these courses and enabling students to undertake systems design after learning chip design. He said the government is looking forward to scale the technical training by partnering with industries and institutes such as the Industrial Technology Research Institute of Taiwan. He said these institutions can help set up facilities that can train technicians.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | National 65 EAM S Jaishankar says, India firmly committed to Bhutan’s progress
national_raw_news.content: External Affairs Minister Dr. S Jaishankar has said that India stands firmly committed to Bhutan’s progress and prosperity. He joined Bhutan Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay and Foreign Minister DN Dhungyel in launching second phase of international UPI for Bhutanese citizens visiting India. Dr Jaishankar is on a two day visit to Thimpu, Bhutan. In a social media post, he said that together with the use of UPI in Bhutan, this completes two-way UPI-based digital payment connectivity between India and Bhutan. They also witnessed exchange of MoU on extending the Nehru Wangchuck Scholarship Scheme for higher education by Bhutanese students at Indian institutions. Dr Jaishankar termed this a step forward for India-Bhutan cooperation in education and capacity building. The External Affairs Minister also handed over 54 Made in India electric vehicles to Prime Minister Tobgay. The Minister said India is supporting Bhutan’s advances towards e-mobility and sustainability transport. Earlier, Dr Jaishankar called on the Bhutan Prime Minister, saying that he deeply values Mr Tobgay’s sentiments for India-Bhutan unique ties of friendship and cooperation. Yesterday, Dr. Jaishankar received a warm welcome from his Bhutanese counterpart D N Dhungyel on his arrival in the valley town of Paro. The talks between the two ministers focused on advancing multifaceted engagement in development partnership, energy, trade, connectivity, culture and people-to-people ties. He also inaugurated a couple of projects, including a 65-bed Gyaltsuen Jetsun Pema Mother and Child Hospital in Mongar. He also laid the foundation stone for the 500 KW Lunana Hydropower Project in Gasa, northern Bhutan.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | National 47 India asserts to take all necessary steps to ensure energy security after US passes bill
national_raw_news.content: The government today said that it will take all necessary steps to protect its economic interests and ensure energy security. The External Affairs Ministry said that country remains firmly committed to ensuring energy security for its 140 crore people and will continue to do so through diversified sourcing and on the basis of evolving market dynamics. The statement came amid the passing of a bill by the US House of Representative that will allow US President Donald Trump to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on countries such as India and China for procuring Russian crude oil. The Ministry said that this issue has been discussed at high levels in recent months with various US interlocutors. Its potential implications for not just the bilateral relationship but also the international energy market have been very clearly articulated by the Indian side. The Ministry said that the Indian side has also made clear its determination to take all necessary measures to protect its trade and economic interests. The government made it clear that it will work closely with Indian trade and industry bodies to deal with the implications of these developments. The sanctions bill was passed by the US Senate last month. The House of Representatives passed the bill in a 262-159 vote last evening. It will become a law once US President signs it. The bill seeks to impose sanctions not only on Russia’s leadership and energy sector, but also on the shadow fleet of vessels that enable Moscow to evade sanctions on oil deliveries. It also seeks to authorise US President to impose stiff tariffs on China, India and other countries to reduce their dependence on Russian oil and gas, as well as additional sanctions on Iran.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | National 158 Month-long Seva Sankalp Abhiyaan begins marking PM Modi’s 25 yrs in public service
national_raw_news.content: BJP’s month-long nationwide Seva Sankalp Abhiyaan has begun from today to mark the completion of 25 years of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s public life and service. As part of the Seva Sankalp Abhiyaan which will continue till 17th of next month, the first day of the campaign is being observed as Seva Diwas, under which blood donation camps have been organised across the country. Party President Nitin Nabin inaugurated blood donation camp at the Party Headquarters in New Delhi. Mr Nabin along with other party leaders and workers also donated blood. Later talking to media on the occasion, BJP chief said, party workers across the country are participating in these blood donation camp. He noted that under the leadership of the Prime Minister Modi lives of the citizens have been transformed. Mr Nabin said under the leadership of Prime Minister Modi, India is rapidly moving on the path of development to achieve the goal of Viksit Bharat by 2047. In Delhi, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta performed hawan at Khatu Shyam temple. Later talking to media, Ms Gupta said that she wished for Prime Minister’s long life and good health. She added that, inspired by Mr Modi’s constant emphasis on public service, Delhi government has organised various government-led programs today.

national_raw_news.title: Meghalaya hosts North East Inter-State Badminton Championship ahead of National Games 2027 7 hours ago 90
national_raw_news.content: The North East Zone Inter-State Badminton Championship 2026 has returned to Meghalaya for the first time since 2016. The tournament serves as the official qualifying ground for the team events of the highly anticipated National Games 2027 in the state. Underway at the Jawaharlal Nehru Indoor Sports Complex, Shillong, the championship will continue till 19th September 2026. More than 250 top-tier shuttlers representing all eight Northeastern states – Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Manipur, Nagaland, Tripura, and Sikkim have come together for the championship. Wailadmiki Shylla, Minister of Sports and Youth Affairs, Government of Meghalaya said that the return of this important championship to Shillong after ten long years arrives at a highly opportune moment, as Meghalaya prepares to host the 39th National Games next year. He added that the State witnessed a surge in the Sports budget from a mere ₹40 crore eight to nine years ago to a staggering ₹844 crore. The objective of the funding is to provide better infrastructure, platforms, and opportunities for the youth, alongside a hike in prize money that now awards ₹2 lakh to National Games gold medallists. Furthermore, Shylla underscored the transformative Meghalaya Outstanding Direct Appointment Policy, which guarantees direct government jobs to State athletes who secure medals at major events. The policy also allows athletes a grace period of up to ten years to pursue higher education or advance their sporting careers before taking up their appointed posts. Turning to National Games preparations, he confirmed that a dedicated stipend will be provided to the final selected team to support their ongoing training. Ace shuttler Ashmita Chaliha, the first Indian ever to win the Korea Masters Title, who is representing Assam in the tournament, commended the sports momentum as she returned to compete in Shillong at the North East Inter-State Badminton Championship after nearly a decade. Expressing optimism regarding the host State’s venue readiness and infrastructure build-up for the upcoming National Games next year, Chaliha highlighted the rise of grassroots talent across the region. She observed that while young shuttlers are emerging through structured training, grooming and high-level match exposure will be essential to bridge the gap with elite circuits. Offering a message to Meghalaya’s athletes, she urged them to play without the burden of expectations. Beyond the competition, the successful hosting of the championship underscores a larger milestone for Meghalaya. As the State prepares to host the 39th National Games next year, hosting a premier regional event of this scale functions as a practical demonstration of Shillong’s operational readiness.

national_raw_news.title: Domestic markets end flat 6 hours ago 177
national_raw_news.content: Benchmark domestic equity indices today ended almost flat. The Sensex dipped 22 points to close at 74,315. The Nifty added 53 points to settle at 23,271. In the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index gained 0.9 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index added 0.8 per cent. Earlier, the markets opened mildly lower after a hawkish stance from the US Federal Reserve and concerns over geopolitical developments. However, both the indices soon recovered and traded with gains for most of the volatile session, supported by value buying. In the Sensex pack, 21 out of 30 companies logged gains. Among the top performers, Tata Steel climbed 2.8 per cent, Bharat Electronics Limited surged 2.4 per cent and Indigo gained 2.3 per cent. In contrast, HDFC Bank declined 1.3 per cent, Titan dipped over 1.1 per cent and ICICI Bank fell one per cent. In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 18 out of 28 sectors edged upward. Among the top gainers, Insurance advanced 3.2 per cent, Capital Goods jumped nearly two per cent, and Industrials gained one and a half per cent. In contrast, Top 10 Banks declined 0.7 per cent, Private Banks Index shed 0.6 per cent and Bankex dropped half a per cent. The overall market breadth at the BSE was positive, as shares of 2 thousand 686 companies advanced, 1 thousand 642 declined and 207 remained unchanged.
